prompt: Which of the four parts does no work at all?
hint: People call it a component because it is the largest object in the case.

choices.text: the motherboard, which connects the other three
choices.why: It calculates nothing and remembers nothing.

choices.text: the memory, which only holds what is given to it
choices.why: Holding is work, and it is the fast kind.

choices.text: the storage, which only keeps what is written
choices.why: Keeping is its work, and it is the durable kind.

choices.text: the power supply, which converts and hands out
choices.why: Converting is work, and it is not one of the four.

prompt: A program runs slower on a new six-core machine than on an old one. What explains it?
hint: Only one of the two processor numbers grew over twenty years.

choices.text: the new machine has to schedule across six cores
choices.why: Scheduling costs nothing at this scale.

choices.text: six cores share the memory bandwidth between themselves
choices.why: They do, and one program does not notice.

choices.text: the old machine had been optimised over several years
choices.why: Nothing about the machine improves with age.

choices.text: it runs on just one of them, and that one is not as fast
choices.why: Cores grew and the clock did not.

prompt: The whole machine is slow, the storage light is busy and the processor is idle. What is that?
hint: The giveaway is that switching between windows hurts most.

choices.text: a program that is using the network heavily
choices.why: The storage light would say nothing about it.

choices.text: a disk that is beginning to fail mechanically
choices.why: That is slow on particular files, not on switching.

choices.text: a processor that is thermally throttling
choices.why: Throttling keeps the processor busy at a lower speed.

choices.text: swapping, because memory has filled up
choices.why: The worker is carrying paper, not working.

prompt: Why is an SSD the upgrade that makes an old machine feel new?

choices.text: it raises the clock speed that the processor is able to hold
choices.why: Storage decides nothing about the clock.

choices.text: reaching a thing falls from ten milliseconds to a tenth
choices.why: The processor is the same; the distance changed.

choices.text: it doubles the memory available to the system
choices.why: It adds no memory at all.

choices.text: it removes the need for the machine to swap at all any more
choices.why: Swapping still happens; it merely hurts less.

prompt: Scaled so a nanosecond is a second, what is a hard disk read?
hint: The SSD in the same scale is a day and a half.

choices.text: four days at most
choices.why: That is far too close to the SSD.

choices.text: four months
choices.why: Against two minutes for memory and a day and a half for an SSD.

choices.text: four years and a bit
choices.why: Longer than the figure the lesson gives.

choices.text: four hours or so
choices.why: That would make the hierarchy almost flat.

prompt: `32 GB RAM · 1 TB HDD` on a budget machine. What is wrong with it?
hint: Ask the three questions in order and one of them fails.

choices.text: a terabyte is far more storage than almost anybody needs
choices.why: Capacity is not the complaint.

choices.text: thirty-two gigabytes will not fit on a budget machine board
choices.why: It fits, and that is why it is offered.

choices.text: the big number is on the part that matters least here
choices.why: Twice the memory needed, on ten-millisecond storage.

choices.text: the two parts are from different generations
choices.why: Nothing in the line says so.

prompt: What is the difference between a processor and a graphics processor?

choices.text: one runs programs and the other only drivers
choices.why: Both run programs written for them.

choices.text: one is built for pictures and the other one is built for arithmetic
choices.why: Both do arithmetic; pictures were the first bulk job.

choices.text: one does hard things in sequence, the other easy ones at once
choices.why: Thousands of simple cores against a dozen complicated ones.

choices.text: one is on the board and the other on a card
choices.why: A graphics processor is often on the same chip.

prompt: A card is described as `8 GB`. What is that number?

choices.text: the largest texture the card is able to hold
choices.why: It is a total, not a limit on one thing.

choices.text: the amount of memory the card needs the machine to have
choices.why: No such requirement is stated that way.

choices.text: the card's own memory, beside the machine's
choices.why: Running out of it drops the frame rate off a cliff.

choices.text: a share of the machine memory reserved for it
choices.why: That is what integrated graphics does instead.

prompt: Somebody cannot name anything from the demanding list. What follows about a graphics card?
hint: The lesson puts these four components together for a reason.

choices.text: it costs three times: the card, the supply and the cooling
choices.why: And it is no faster at anything they do.

choices.text: it will make the machine quieter under office work
choices.why: It makes heat, and heat makes noise.

choices.text: it is still worth it for running several monitors
choices.why: Screens are a connector question, not a performance one.

choices.text: it future-proofs the machine for the next four or five years
choices.why: It buys performance nobody in this case uses.

prompt: Why is a cheap power supply a different kind of risk from a cheap anything else?

choices.text: it is the only part with no warranty of its own
choices.why: They are warranted like anything else.

choices.text: its failure is not contained to itself
choices.why: It can put the wrong voltage onto everything attached.

choices.text: it cannot be replaced without replacing the board
choices.why: It is one of the easiest parts to replace.

choices.text: it is the component most likely to fail first
choices.why: Not the argument the lesson makes.

prompt: Components add up to about 400 W. What supply does the lesson point at?
hint: Headroom is a band rather than a direction.

choices.text: about 550 W, which is roughly thirty per cent more
choices.why: Spikes, and the efficiency band near half load.

choices.text: about 450 W, which is a comfortable ten per cent more
choices.why: Too little for the spikes the lesson describes.

choices.text: exactly 400 W, since that is what they draw
choices.why: A supply at its limit shuts down rather than sag.

choices.text: 1000 W, because more headroom is always the safer choice
choices.why: It then sits at 20% load, where it is least efficient.

prompt: A machine is fast for ten minutes and then slower, and recovers when left alone. What is it?
hint: The fans are loud before the slowdown, not after.

choices.text: a memory fault that appears under sustained load
choices.why: Memory crashes and corrupts; it does not taper.

choices.text: thermal throttling, whose commonest cause is dust
choices.why: A genuinely slow machine is slow from the first second.

choices.text: a disk that is heating up and retrying reads
choices.why: A disk pauses on files rather than slowing everything.

choices.text: a power supply that cannot hold the load for long
choices.why: That restarts rather than slows.

prompt: A keyboard types the wrong characters. Where does the problem live?

choices.text: in the application, which is interpreting them
choices.why: Every application would have to be wrong at once.

choices.text: in the layout setting, which is software
choices.why: The printing on the keys decides nothing.

choices.text: in the cable, which is failing intermittently
choices.why: A failing cable drops keys; it does not translate them.

choices.text: in the keyboard's own firmware, which needs updating
choices.why: The keyboard sends positions, not letters.

prompt: Which number on a monitor box actually decides how much fits on screen?

choices.text: the resolution, read together with the size
choices.why: The two together are the density that matters.

choices.text: the refresh rate the panel is driven at, in hertz
choices.why: That is how often the picture is redrawn.

choices.text: the panel technology, whether IPS or VA or TN
choices.why: That decides colour and angle, not how much fits.

choices.text: the diagonal of the panel, measured in inches
choices.why: Bigger at the same resolution means larger, not more.

prompt: Why is a printer the one device in this lesson sold at a loss?

choices.text: printers are built from parts nobody else wants
choices.why: Nothing about the parts explains the price.

choices.text: the money is in the consumable it then requires
choices.why: The arithmetic is per page, not per machine.

choices.text: the software that drives it is licensed separately
choices.why: The driver is given away.

choices.text: the maker recovers it on the warranty contract
choices.why: Warranties are not where it is recovered.

prompt: A scanner is advertised at `4800 × 9600 dpi`. What should you read?
hint: One of the two axes is moved by a motor rather than sampled.

choices.text: the product of the two, which is the pixel count
choices.why: They are not multiplied into anything meaningful.

choices.text: neither, since dpi says nothing about a scanner
choices.why: Optical dpi says a great deal.

choices.text: the smaller number, and only if it is optical
choices.why: The larger one is the stepper motor, not the sensor.

choices.text: the larger number, which is the real resolution
choices.why: That is the number the box wants you to read.

prompt: What is a peripheral, stated as the lesson states it?

choices.text: a device the operating system needs a driver for
choices.why: Most need none any more.

choices.text: anything connected by a cable rather than a slot
choices.why: Plenty of peripherals are wireless.

choices.text: a translator between a person and a machine
choices.why: Which is why its failures are at the edges.

choices.text: any device that is not inside the case
choices.why: A description of where, not of what.

prompt: Why does a higher DPI not make a better mouse?

choices.text: a high setting drains the battery of a wireless mouse faster
choices.why: A minor effect, and not the argument.

choices.text: it is sensitivity, and most people then turn it down
choices.why: Quality is the sensor, the switches and the feet.

choices.text: the operating system quietly caps it at a much lower value
choices.why: It does not cap it.

choices.text: the number is invented by each manufacturer
choices.why: It is measurable, and it is simply not quality.

prompt: A port is three promises wearing one shape. Which three?

choices.text: the speed, the length and the direction of travel
choices.why: Length is a cable property.

choices.text: the shape, the speed and what travels down it

choices.text: the shape, the colour and the standard it is named for
choices.why: Colour is a convention and often absent.

prompt: A USB-C cable charges a laptop but will not carry a monitor. Why is that normal?

choices.text: video needs a cable shorter than a metre

choices.text: power and video are separate negotiations on one shape

choices.text: the monitor needs the cable the other way round

choices.text: a cable can carry either the power or the video, never both
choices.why: Many carry both.

prompt: A monitor has both HDMI and DisplayPort. Which does the lesson prefer, and why?

choices.text: whichever cable came in the box with the monitor

choices.text: neither; on a monitor the two are identical

choices.text: DisplayPort, for higher refresh rates at high resolution

prompt: Two machines and a cable that only works in one direction. What kind of adapter is it?

choices.text: a certified one, which enforces the direction
